P R A C T I C E M AT E R I A L



Drive Train
Pop Quizzes
7 quizzes — one per course — 10 multiple-choice questions each, 70 questions total.


     How to use these quizzes
     Take one quiz at a time, closed book. Circle your answer for each question. Every question is tagged with
     the module it tests, so a miss points straight back to what to review.

     Target: 9 / 10 before moving on to the next course. If you score below 9, review the missed modules
     and retake the quiz.

     Answer key is separate. No answers appear after the individual quizzes. All answers are grouped in a
     separate Answer Key section at the very back, after a clear page break, so you can print the quizzes
     without the answers.

Quiz 1 — Complete Clutch Essentials
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Clutch System Principles
       Multi-Plate Clutch Systems
       Dual Mass Flywheel Design and Operation
       Conventional Clutch Diagnostics

CLUTCH SYSTEM PRINCIPLES
1. What is the main purpose of the clutch in a manual transmission vehicle?
    A. To increase engine power at high speed
    B. To connect and disconnect engine drive to the transmission so gears can be changed and the vehicle can
    stop with the engine running
    C. To cool the transmission oil
    D. To charge the battery while driving
CLUTCH SYSTEM PRINCIPLES
2. In a typical single-plate clutch, the friction disc is splined to which part and clamped between which
two parts?
    A. The crankshaft; the gearbox casing and bell housing
    B. The transmission input shaft; the flywheel and the pressure plate
    C. The driveshaft; the differential and axle
    D. The release bearing; the pedal and cable
CLUTCH SYSTEM PRINCIPLES
3. What does a diaphragm spring in the pressure plate do when the clutch pedal is pressed?
    A. It clamps the disc harder to the flywheel
    B. Its fingers are pushed in, pulling the pressure plate away so the disc is released
    C. It locks the differential
    D. It pumps hydraulic fluid to the brakes
M U LT I - P L AT E C L U T C H S Y S T E M S
4. Why use a multi-plate clutch instead of a single-plate clutch?
    A. It needs no release bearing
    B. More friction surfaces transmit more torque in a compact size
    C. It eliminates the flywheel
    D. It works without any friction material
M U LT I - P L AT E C L U T C H S Y S T E M S
5. A wet multi-plate clutch differs from a dry multi-plate clutch because it:
    A. Runs in oil, which cools the plates and gives smoother, longer-lasting engagement
    B. Has no plates at all
    C. Only works on electric vehicles
    D. Uses air pressure to clamp the plates


Quiz 1 — Complete Clutch Essentials                                                                 Page 1 of 2
Quiz 1 — continued
D U A L M A S S F LY W H E E L D E S I G N A N D O P E R AT I O N
6. What is the main job of a dual mass flywheel (DMF)?
    A. To increase top speed
    B. To absorb and damp engine torsional vibration before it reaches the gearbox
    C. To double the clutch clamping force
    D. To replace the starter motor
D U A L M A S S F LY W H E E L D E S I G N A N D O P E R AT I O N
7. Inside a DMF, the primary and secondary masses are connected by:
    A. A rigid solid bolted joint with no movement
    B. Arc springs that allow controlled relative movement between the masses
    C. A rubber drive belt
    D. Hydraulic fluid only
D U A L M A S S F LY W H E E L D E S I G N A N D O P E R AT I O N
8. Which symptom most points to a worn or failing DMF?
    A. A flat tire vibration at motorway speed only
    B. Rattle or knocking at idle and on start-up/shut-down, with vibration through the vehicle
    C. The headlights flickering
    D. Low engine oil pressure
CONVENTIONAL CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
9. A clutch is slipping. Which test result confirms slip?
    A. Engine RPM rises under load in a high gear but road speed does not rise with it
    B. The pedal feels very heavy
    C. First gear is hard to select at a standstill
    D. The release bearing is noisy with the pedal up
CONVENTIONAL CLUTCH DIAGNOSTICS
10. A clutch drags (does not fully release), often due to air in the hydraulic system or incorrect
adjustment. The driver will most likely report:
    A. Difficulty selecting first and reverse gear, with crunching
    B. The engine overheating
    C. A slipping clutch smell at high speed
    D. Loss of power steering

End of Quiz 1. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 2 — Manual Transmission Explained
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Manual Transmission Operation
       Understanding Manual Transaxles

M A N U A L T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N
1. Why does a vehicle need different gear ratios?
    A. To keep the radio tuned to different stations
    B. To multiply engine torque for pulling away and allow higher road speed with lower engine load as speed
    rises
    C. To change the direction of the exhaust
    D. To recharge the gearbox oil
M A N U A L T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N
2. In a constant-mesh manual gearbox, the gear pairs are:
    A. Only meshed when the driver moves the gear lever
    B. Always in mesh; drive is locked in by dog teeth / synchromesh hubs sliding onto the selected gear
    C. Driven by a rubber belt
    D. Connected by a chain only in reverse
M A N U A L T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N
3. What does the synchromesh (synchronizer) do during a gear change?
    A. It cools the gear oil
    B. It uses friction to match the speed of the gear and shaft before the dog teeth engage, preventing
    crunching
    C. It locks both axles together
    D. It measures road speed
M A N U A L T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N
4. How is reverse gear usually obtained in a manual gearbox?
    A. By reversing engine rotation
    B. By adding an idler gear that reverses the direction of the output shaft
    C. By turning the steering wheel fully
    D. By switching the clutch off
M A N U A L T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N
5. Worn synchromesh on second gear will most likely cause:
    A. Crunching when changing into second gear, especially when rushed or cold
    B. The clutch to slip in fifth gear
    C. Loss of reverse gear only
    D. The speedometer to stop working




Quiz 2 — Manual Transmission Explained                                                                     Page 1 of 2
Quiz 2 — continued
U N D E R S TA N D I N G M A N U A L T R A N S A X L E S
6. A transaxle differs from a separate transmission and final drive because it:
    A. Has no gears at all
    B. Combines the gearbox, final drive, and differential in one housing
    C. Is only used on rear-wheel-drive trucks
    D. Uses no lubricant
U N D E R S TA N D I N G M A N U A L T R A N S A X L E S
7. Manual transaxles are most commonly used on:
    A. Front-wheel-drive cars, where the engine and driven wheels are at the same end
    B. Steam locomotives
    C. Aircraft
    D. Rear-engine buses only
U N D E R S TA N D I N G M A N U A L T R A N S A X L E S
8. In a front-wheel-drive transaxle, power leaves the differential to the wheels through:
    A. A long propshaft to the rear axle
    B. Drive shafts (half shafts) with constant velocity joints
    C. A chain drive to each wheel
    D. The steering rack
U N D E R S TA N D I N G M A N U A L T R A N S A X L E S
9. Why must the correct specified oil be used in a manual transaxle?
    A. The same oil often lubricates both the gears and the differential, and the wrong grade/additives can harm
    synchromesh and bearings
    B. Oil type makes no difference in any gearbox
    C. To change the colour of the casing
    D. Only automatic transmissions need oil
U N D E R S TA N D I N G M A N U A L T R A N S A X L E S
10. A transaxle whines in all gears and the noise changes with road speed, not engine speed in a single
gear. This most likely points to:
    A. Worn clutch release bearing
    B. Final drive / differential or wheel-side components in the transaxle
    C. A slipping drive belt
    D. Low coolant level

End of Quiz 2. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 3 — Dual Clutch Transmission Essentials
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

  Modules Covered
      Introducing DCT

INTRODUCING DCT
1. A dual clutch transmission (DCT) is best described as:
   A. An automatic with only one clutch and a torque converter
   B. Two manual sub-transmissions in one unit, one for odd gears and one for even gears, each with its own
   clutch
   C. A CVT with a belt and pulleys
   D. A manual gearbox with no clutches
INTRODUCING DCT
2. How does a DCT achieve such fast gear changes?
   A. The driver changes gear twice as fast
   B. The next gear is preselected on the other sub-transmission, so the change is a swap of clutches
   C. It skips every second gear
   D. It turns the engine off during the shift
INTRODUCING DCT
3. In a DCT, while first gear is driving through clutch 1, the control system will normally:
   A. Leave all other gears disengaged
   B. Preselect second gear on the other sub-transmission ready for the upshift
   C. Preselect reverse gear
   D. Disconnect the engine completely
INTRODUCING DCT
4. A wet-clutch DCT differs from a dry-clutch DCT because the wet type:
   A. Cannot be used in cars
   B. Runs its clutches in oil, handling higher torque and heat better, at some cost to efficiency
   C. Has no mechatronics unit
   D. Only has two gears
INTRODUCING DCT
5. What is the mechatronics unit in a DCT?
   A. The driver's gear lever
   B. The combined hydraulic/electronic control unit that operates the clutches and shift actuators from TCM
   commands
   C. A second engine
   D. The parking brake module




Quiz 3 — Dual Clutch Transmission Essentials                                                            Page 1 of 2
Quiz 3 — continued
INTRODUCING DCT
6. Why can a DCT feel hesitant or jerky at very low speed and in stop-start traffic?
   A. It has no first gear
   B. Clutches are being slipped to creep like a torque converter, and repeated low-speed slipping builds heat
   C. The belt stretches at low speed
   D. It only works above 30 mph
INTRODUCING DCT
7. What does DCT clutch overheating protection most likely do?
   A. Turns off the headlights
   B. Warns the driver and may limit clutch slip, change shift strategy, or disengage drive until temperatures fall
   C. Increases clutch slip deliberately
   D. Locks the steering
INTRODUCING DCT
8. Compared with a conventional torque-converter automatic, a DCT generally offers:
   A. Slower shifts and higher fuel use
   B. Fast shifts and good efficiency because there is a direct mechanical connection, with no torque converter
   slip in normal driving
   C. No gear changes at all
   D. Unlimited creep with no wear
INTRODUCING DCT
9. A DCT will not engage drive and stores clutch actuator faults. The best first checks are:
   A. Tire pressures and wheel alignment
   B. DCT fluid level/condition, mechatronics supply and grounds, and scan data for clutch
   position/temperature
   C. Engine coolant colour only
   D. The radio fuse
INTRODUCING DCT
10. Why is the specified DCT fluid and service interval especially important?
   A. The same fluid may cool/lubricate clutches and operate the mechatronics, so wrong or degraded fluid
   affects shift quality and clutch control
   B. Fluid never affects a DCT
   C. Any engine oil works the same
   D. DCTs are sealed and contain no fluid

End of Quiz 3. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 4 — Mastering Automatic Transmissions
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Automatic Transmission Operations
       Torque Converter Operations
       Planetary Gear Sets
       Automatic Transmission Hydraulics
       Automatic Transmission Fluids
       Electronic Transmission Control

A U TO M AT I C T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N S
1. In a conventional automatic transmission, gear changes are made by:
    A. The driver sliding gears along a shaft by hand
    B. Applying and releasing clutches and brakes (bands/multi-plate packs) to change which planetary
    members are held or driven
    C. Moving a belt between pulleys
    D. Turning the torque converter around
A U TO M AT I C T R A N S M I S S I O N O P E R AT I O N S
2. What does the 'P' (Park) position engage that the other positions do not?
    A. The torque converter lock-up clutch
    B. A parking pawl that mechanically locks the output shaft
    C. The highest gear
    D. The radiator fan
TO R Q U E C O N V E R T E R O P E R AT I O N S
3. The three main elements inside a torque converter are:
    A. Ring gear, planet gears, and carrier
    B. Impeller (pump), turbine, and stator
    C. Rotor, stator, and brushes
    D. Input shaft, layshaft, and mainshaft
TO R Q U E C O N V E R T E R O P E R AT I O N S
4. What does the stator do at low speed / high slip in a torque converter?
    A. It disconnects the engine
    B. It redirects fluid returning from the turbine so the converter multiplies torque
    C. It locks the converter solid
    D. It cools the fluid in the radiator
P L A N E TA RY G E A R S E T S
5. A simple planetary gear set consists of:
    A. Two bevel gears and a cross pin
    B. A sun gear, planet gears on a carrier, and an outer ring (annulus) gear
    C. A worm and a wheel
    D. A chain and two sprockets
Quiz 4 — Mastering Automatic Transmissions                                                              Page 1 of 2
Quiz 4 — continued
P L A N E TA RY G E A R S E T S
6. In a planetary set, different ratios (including reverse and overdrive) are obtained by:
    A. Changing the size of the gears while driving
    B. Holding one member, driving another, and taking output from the third in different combinations
    C. Adding more fluid
    D. Reversing the engine
A U TO M AT I C T R A N S M I S S I O N H Y D R A U L I C S
7. What is the main role of the hydraulic system and valve body in a conventional automatic?
    A. To steer the vehicle
    B. To direct pressurised fluid to apply/release the correct clutches and brakes for each gear, and to control
    shift pressure and feel
    C. To pump fuel to the engine
    D. To operate the windshield wipers
A U TO M AT I C T R A N S M I S S I O N H Y D R A U L I C S
8. Line pressure that is too low will most likely cause:
    A. Harsh, violent shifts only
    B. Clutch/band slip, delayed or flared shifts, and rapid friction wear
    C. The engine to stall at idle every time
    D. Loss of brake pressure
A U TO M AT I C T R A N S M I S S I O N F L U I D S
9. Why must the exact specified ATF be used?
    A. All ATF is identical, so it does not matter
    B. Friction characteristics, viscosity, and additives differ; the wrong ATF can cause shudder, harsh or slipping
    shifts, and damage
    C. Only the colour matters
    D. ATF is the same as engine oil
ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION CONTROL
10. The transmission control module (TCM) decides shift points mainly from inputs such as:
    A. Radio volume and seat position
    B. Engine load/throttle, vehicle speed, engine and fluid temperatures, and driver demand
    C. Tire tread depth only
    D. Windshield washer level

End of Quiz 4. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.




Quiz 4 — Mastering Automatic Transmissions                                                                Page 2 of 2
Quiz 5 — CVT Fundamentals
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Continuously Variable Transmission Overview

C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
1. A continuously variable transmission (CVT) differs from a stepped automatic because it:
    A. Has only neutral and reverse
    B. Provides a seamless range of ratios with no fixed gear steps
    C. Uses a manual clutch pedal
    D. Has exactly three forward gears
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
2. In the most common automotive CVT, ratio is changed by:
    A. Sliding gears along a splined shaft
    B. Moving the sides of two variable-diameter pulleys so the belt/chain rides higher on one and lower on the
    other
    C. Switching planetary members on and off
    D. Changing tire size while driving
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
3. The drive element between the CVT pulleys is usually:
    A. A multi-plate clutch pack
    B. A steel push belt or a chain designed for the pulleys
    C. A rubber V-belt like an accessory drive belt on most car CVTs
    D. A set of bevel gears
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
4. Why does a CVT improve fuel economy in normal driving?
    A. It removes the engine from the car
    B. It lets the engine stay near its most efficient speed for the load instead of being tied to fixed gear steps
    C. It turns the engine off at all speeds
    D. It makes the vehicle lighter
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
5. Many CVTs use a torque converter or start clutch at low speed mainly to:
    A. Provide smooth pull-away and creep, and isolate vibration at a standstill
    B. Lock the differential
    C. Charge the battery
    D. Cool the belt




Quiz 5 — CVT Fundamentals                                                                                   Page 1 of 2
Quiz 5 — continued
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
6. Why is the specified CVT fluid critical and not interchangeable with regular ATF?
    A. CVT fluid is only a different colour
    B. It must provide the exact metal-to-metal friction between belt/chain and pulleys plus hydraulic control;
    wrong fluid can cause belt slip and pulley damage
    C. CVTs contain no fluid
    D. Any gear oil gives the same result
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
7. A CVT vehicle shudders on pull-away and the fluid is dark and burnt-smelling. The most likely
concern is:
    A. Normal operation needing no checks
    B. Belt/chain slip and wear from degraded fluid or low pressure — check fluid, pressures, and scan data
    before condemning the unit
    C. A flat spot on a tire
    D. Low windshield washer fluid
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
8. What protects a CVT if the belt begins to slip excessively?
    A. Nothing — slip has no effect
    B. Control strategies raise clamping pressure and may limit engine torque / enter a limp mode to prevent
    pulley damage
    C. The driver must select Park immediately in all cases
    D. The pulleys lock together permanently
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
9. The 'rubber band' feel drivers report in some CVTs is:
    A. A slipping accessory belt
    B. Engine RPM rising and holding while vehicle speed catches up, because ratio changes separately from
    road speed
    C. The tires stretching under load
    D. A faulty accelerator cable in all cases
C O N T I N U O U S LY VA R I A B L E T R A N S M I S S I O N O V E RV I E W
10. Some CVTs offer simulated 'steps' in manual/sport mode. These are:
    A. Real additional fixed gears fitted inside
    B. Programmed pulley ratio jumps that imitate stepped shifts for driver feel
    C. Changes to the final drive gearing
    D. Produced by the torque converter only

End of Quiz 5. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 6 — Introducing Transfer Cases
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Transfer Case Overview

T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
1. What is the main purpose of a transfer case?
    A. To boost engine power
    B. To split drive between the front and rear axles on four-wheel-drive / all-wheel-drive vehicles
    C. To replace the main gearbox
    D. To operate the parking brake
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
2. Where is the transfer case normally fitted?
    A. In front of the engine
    B. Behind (after) the main transmission, before the front and rear propshafts
    C. Inside the fuel tank
    D. On the steering column
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
3. What does low range (4L) provide compared with high range (4H)?
    A. Higher top speed
    B. A deep extra reduction — much more wheel torque at lower speed for climbing, towing, and off-road work
    C. No drive to the front axle
    D. Automatic tire inflation
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
4. Inside many transfer cases, drive to one output is carried by:
    A. A timing belt
    B. A wide chain (or gear drive) between the input and the second output shaft
    C. A hydraulic motor only
    D. The exhaust system
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
5. Part-time 4WD with a locked centre (no centre differential action) should not be used on dry paved
roads because:
    A. It uses too much fuel only
    B. Front and rear axles are forced to turn at the same speed, causing driveline wind-up, tire scrub, and
    strain in turns
    C. It disengages the brakes
    D. It overheats the radio




Quiz 6 — Introducing Transfer Cases                                                                     Page 1 of 2
Quiz 6 — continued
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
6. What is driveline wind-up (binding)?
    A. A loose propshaft bolt
    B. Torsional stress built up when front and rear wheels are forced to rotate at different-path speeds with no
    centre differential to allow it
    C. A worn wheel bearing noise
    D. The transfer case oil foaming
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
7. An electronically controlled transfer case changes range/mode using:
    A. The driver's hand on a lever in all modern cases
    B. An electric shift motor/actuator commanded by a control module, often with position sensors to confirm
    the shift
    C. Engine vacuum only
    D. The ABS pump
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
8. A transfer case will not shift into low range. A common requirement that must be met first is:
    A. Vehicle at motorway speed
    B. Vehicle stopped or nearly stopped, transmission in Neutral, foot brake applied (per manufacturer
    procedure)
    C. Headlights switched on
    D. Fuel tank full
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
9. Why is the specified transfer case fluid and level important?
    A. It only affects the paint on the casing
    B. The chain, bearings, clutches, and shift components rely on it; low or wrong fluid causes noise, poor
    shifting, and wear
    C. Transfer cases are dry inside
    D. Any fluid level is acceptable
T R A N S F E R C A S E O V E RV I E W
10. A vehicle with an active (on-demand) transfer case mainly drives one axle and engages the other
when:
    A. The headlights are on
    B. Wheel slip or driving conditions are detected and the module applies a clutch pack to send torque to the
    second axle
    C. The driver opens a door
    D. Engine temperature is low only

End of Quiz 6. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Quiz 7 — Understanding Final Drives
Name: ________________________________ Date: ________________ Score: ___ / 10

   Modules Covered
       Understanding Final Drives
       Limited Slip Differentials
       Drive Shaft Universal and Consistent Velocity Joint Operation

U N D E R S TA N D I N G F I N A L D R I V E S
1. The final drive performs two main jobs. They are:
    A. Cooling the engine and charging the battery
    B. Providing the last gear reduction and, through the differential, turning drive through 90 degrees on a
    conventional rear axle while allowing wheels to turn at different speeds
    C. Filtering the oil and pumping fuel
    D. Locking both wheels permanently together
U N D E R S TA N D I N G F I N A L D R I V E S
2. A final drive ratio of 4.1:1 means:
    A. The wheels turn 4.1 times for each propshaft turn
    B. The pinion/propshaft turns 4.1 times for each turn of the ring gear and wheels
    C. Top speed is 4.1 mph
    D. There are 4.1 gears in the axle
U N D E R S TA N D I N G F I N A L D R I V E S
3. Why does an open differential allow the driven wheels to turn at different speeds in a turn?
    A. It disconnects one wheel completely
    B. Its planet pinions rotate on their pin, dividing speed between the side gears while still delivering drive
    C. It locks the axles with a chain
    D. It changes the final drive ratio
U N D E R S TA N D I N G F I N A L D R I V E S
4. Incorrect ring gear and pinion backlash / contact pattern after axle work will most likely cause:
    A. Improved fuel economy
    B. Whine or clonk on drive/coast and accelerated gear wear
    C. The clutch to slip
    D. Loss of steering assistance
LIMITED SLIP DIFFERENTIALS
5. A limited slip differential (LSD) improves on an open differential by:
    A. Removing the need for axle oil
    B. Transferring some torque to the wheel with grip when the other wheel starts to spin, instead of sending
    nearly all speed to the spinning wheel
    C. Locking the steering in a straight line
    D. Increasing tire tread depth



Quiz 7 — Understanding Final Drives                                                                         Page 1 of 2
Quiz 7 — continued
LIMITED SLIP DIFFERENTIALS
6. In a clutch-pack LSD, the limiting action comes from:
    A. Brake pads on the wheels
    B. Friction clutch packs compressed as torque is applied (often with preload), resisting a speed difference
    between the wheels
    C. Magnets in the axle tubes
    D. The ABS module only
LIMITED SLIP DIFFERENTIALS
7. A Torsen-type LSD gets its name and action from:
    A. Torque sensing — worm-type gearing that biases torque to the slower, gripping wheel
    B. Temperature sensing in the oil
    C. A torsion bar in the suspension
    D. Total lock at all times
D R I V E S H A F T U N I V E R S A L A N D C O N S I S T E N T V E L O C I T Y J O I N T O P E R AT I O N
8. A single universal (Cardan) joint working at an angle produces:
    A. Perfectly constant output speed
    B. A twice-per-revolution speed fluctuation in the output shaft, which is why joints are phased/paired or CV
    joints are used
    C. No movement at all
    D. Only noise, with no speed change
D R I V E S H A F T U N I V E R S A L A N D C O N S I S T E N T V E L O C I T Y J O I N T O P E R AT I O N
9. A constant velocity (CV) joint differs from a simple UJ because it:
    A. Cannot transmit drive at an angle
    B. Transmits drive at a constant output speed even at an angle, as used on front-wheel-drive shafts
    C. Only works in a straight line
    D. Needs no grease or boot
D R I V E S H A F T U N I V E R S A L A N D C O N S I S T E N T V E L O C I T Y J O I N T O P E R AT I O N
10. A clicking noise on full steering lock at low speed most likely indicates:
    A. A worn outer CV joint, often after a split boot let grease out and dirt/water in
    B. Low engine oil
    C. A slipping clutch
    D. Worn brake pads

End of Quiz 7. Check your score in the separate Answer Key at the back. Target: 9 / 10.

Drive Train Pop Quizzes — Answer Key                                                                    Divider
Answer Key — Quiz 1: Complete Clutch Essentials

Retake date: ________________         Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — The clutch connects/disconnects engine drive for starting, stopping, and gear changes.

2. B — The disc drives the input shaft and is clamped between flywheel and pressure plate.

3. B — Pressing the pedal moves the diaphragm fingers and lifts clamping load to release the disc.

4. B — Stacked plates multiply friction surfaces, giving high torque capacity in a small diameter.

5. A — Wet clutches run in oil for cooling and durability; dry clutches run in air.

6. B — The DMF damps crankshaft torsional pulses, reducing gearbox rattle and vibration.

7. B — Arc springs between the two masses allow movement that absorbs vibration.

8. B — Idle and start/stop rattle plus vibration are classic DMF failure symptoms.

9. A — Rising RPM without matching road speed under load confirms the disc is slipping.

10. A — Incomplete release keeps the input shaft turning, making first/reverse selection hard.




Answer Key — Quiz 1                                                                              Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 2: Manual Transmission Explained

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Low gears multiply torque to pull away; high gears suit cruising speed.

2. B — Constant-mesh gears stay meshed; a sliding hub locks the chosen gear to its shaft.

3. B — Synchromesh matches speeds by friction first, so engagement is smooth and quiet.

4. B — A reverse idler reverses output direction without reversing the engine.

5. A — Worn synchro rings cannot match speeds in time, so second gear crunches.

6. B — A transaxle packages gearbox, final drive, and differential together in one casing.

7. A — Transaxles suit front-wheel drive, keeping the powertrain compact at the driven end.

8. B — Half shafts with CV joints carry drive from the transaxle differential to the front wheels.

9. A — Shared gear/diff oil must suit synchro friction and gear protection — wrong oil causes shift problems.

10. B — Noise tied to road speed across gears points to the final drive/differential side.




Answer Key — Quiz 2                                                                                  Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 3: Dual Clutch Transmission Essentials

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — A DCT splits odd and even gears between two clutches/sub-transmissions.

2. B — Preselection plus a clutch-to-clutch swap gives very fast shifts.

3. B — The idle sub-transmission preselects the likely next gear.

4. B — Oil-cooled wet clutches suit higher torque/heat; dry clutches are simpler and more efficient.

5. B — Mechatronics combines valves, actuators, sensors, and control electronics for the DCT.

6. B — Creeping slips a clutch; sustained creep overheats it, so protection strategies intervene.

7. B — Thermal protection warns and reduces slip/drive until the clutches cool.

8. B — Direct mechanical drive and clutch-swap shifts give DCTs speed and efficiency.

9. B — Fluid, power/grounds, and clutch position/temperature scan data lead DCT diagnosis.

10. A — DCT fluid serves clutches and hydraulics; wrong/degraded fluid harms control and shift feel.




Answer Key — Quiz 3                                                                            Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 4: Mastering Automatic Transmissions

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — Automatics shift by applying/releasing friction elements on planetary members.

2. B — Park adds a pawl locking the output; other ranges are hydraulic/electronic selections.

3. B — Impeller, turbine, and stator are the converter's three main elements.

4. B — At high slip the stator redirects flow to multiply torque; it freewheels near coupling speed.

5. B — Sun, planets/carrier, and ring gear make up a simple planetary set.

6. B — Holding/driving different members gives reduction, direct drive, overdrive, or reverse.

7. B — The valve body routes line pressure to friction elements and controls shift quality.

8. B — Low line pressure cannot clamp friction elements firmly, so they slip and wear.

9. B — ATF friction/viscosity specs are matched to the clutches and controls of each unit.

10. B — Load, speed, temperatures, and demand drive the TCM shift schedule and pressure control.




Answer Key — Quiz 4                                                                              Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 5: CVT Fundamentals

Retake date: ________________         Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — A CVT varies ratio continuously instead of stepping through fixed gears.

2. B — Variable pulleys change effective diameter to vary the ratio seamlessly.

3. B — Car CVTs use a steel push belt or chain matched to the pulley design.

4. B — Continuous ratios keep the engine near its efficient operating point.

5. A — A converter/start clutch gives smooth launch and creep before the belt drive takes over.

6. B — Belt/pulley friction is controlled by the fluid — wrong fluid causes slip and scoring.

7. B — Shudder plus burnt fluid points to slip/wear; verify fluid, pressure, and data first.

8. B — The TCM raises clamping pressure and can limit torque/limp to protect the pulleys.

9. B — RPM flare/hold while speed builds is normal CVT ratio behaviour, within limits.

10. B — Stepped feel is software — the pulleys jump between preset ratios.




Answer Key — Quiz 5                                                                             Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 6: Introducing Transfer Cases

Retake date: ________________        Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — The transfer case distributes drive to front and rear axles.

2. B — It sits after the transmission and feeds both propshafts.

3. B — Low range adds a reduction gear for high torque at low speed.

4. B — Many transfer cases use a chain drive (some use gears) to the second output.

5. B — Locked front/rear speeds on high-grip surfaces cause wind-up and scrub in turns.

6. B — Wind-up is stored torsional load when locked axles travel different distances in a turn.

7. B — Electronic cases use a shift motor and position feedback under module control.

8. B — Most systems require stop/near-stop and Neutral before a low-range shift.

9. B — Correct fluid/level protects the chain, bearings, and any clutch pack inside.

10. B — On-demand systems apply an internal clutch to add the second axle when slip demands it.




Answer Key — Quiz 6                                                                               Separate Key Section
Answer Key — Quiz 7: Understanding Final Drives

Retake date: ________________         Second score: ___ / 10

1. B — The final drive gives the last reduction and the differential splits drive/speed.

2. B — 4.1:1 = propshaft turns 4.1 times per wheel/ring-gear turn.

3. B — Differential pinions walk between side gears to allow a speed difference.

4. B — Wrong backlash/mesh gives noise on drive/coast and rapid wear.

5. B — An LSD biases torque toward the gripping wheel when slip begins.

6. B — Clutch packs, loaded by ramps/preload, resist differential action.

7. A — Torsen = torque sensing; its worm gearing biases torque mechanically.

8. B — An angled UJ speeds and slows the output twice per turn; phasing/CVs cancel it.

9. B — CV joints keep output speed constant through steering/drive angles.

10. A — Clicking on lock is the classic worn outer CV joint symptom, usually after boot failure.

End of Answer Key. Practice Material — Drive Train Pop Quizzes, 7 quizzes, 70 questions.
